item.title: CVE Program Reference Archive Pilot — Preserving the Reference History of CVE Records for the Global Security Community
item.description: CVE Program Reference Archive Pilot — Preserving the Reference History of CVE Records for the Global Security CommunityblogBy CVE Program|November 3, 2026TheCVE™ Programis built on shared, public transparency.CVE Numbering Authorities (CNAs)publishCVE Recordsthat provide foundational information about publicly disclosed vulnerabilities and include references that connect users to additional context, such as vendor advisories, security bulletins, patches, disclosure reports, and other supporting information.Over time, those external references can change or disappear. Websites are reorganized, URLs break, and advisory or patch information may no longer be available at its original location. When that happens, important context associated with a CVE Record can become harder to access and verify.To help address this challenge, the CVE Program is launching the “CVE Program Reference Archive Pilot,” an effort to explore ways to preserve access to vulnerability information referenced by CVE Records.
